summary: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. A scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he served as department head at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1967) and founded the Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality.

Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University. He held posts at Agra (~1958–1962), Pune (~1962–1967), and Deccan College (~1967–1989) as Professor of Applied Linguistics.

Ashoka Welitota is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Senior Lecturer Gr. II at the University of Kelaniya in 2016 and as Senior Lecturer at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ashutosh Mishra earned a Master of Library & Information Science from Central University of Gujarat (2020–2022). He held library posts at the Institute of Rural Management Anand (2022–2024), Bennett University (2024), and Parul University (2024–2026).

Ashutosh Mukherjee studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (BA ~1880–1883). He served at the Calcutta High Court (1904), as Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta (1906–1914), and as President of The Asiatic Society (~1907–1909).

Ashutosh Pareek completed a Ph.D. at Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University (2012). An Indologist, he became a professor at Samrat Prithviraj Chauhan Government College in 2008 and served as visiting faculty at Hindu University of America.

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his Ph.D. under D. Mukherjee at the University of Calcutta in 1967. He was a Senior Research Fellow there (~1968–1971) and a lecturer in English at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Helsinki (1959–1968) under Pentti Aalto, whom he later succeeded. He held positions at the Academy of Finland and was a professor at Helsinki (~1982–2020).
Assa Doron completed a PhD at La Trobe University (2000–2005). Working in Indology and other fields, he was appointed Professor at the Australian National University in 2007.
Astley John Hilary Goodwin was an archaeologist who studied at St. John's College, Selwyn College (1919–1922), and SOAS (1922). He took up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.

Astrid Zotter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Leipzig. She has held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).
Athanaric Huard is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. He held an assistant post at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Athanasius Pryor Treweek studied at the University of Sydney (~1929–1934), where he later served as Professor of Greek from 1938. His fields included linguistics and Indology.

Atsuhiko Yoshida studied at Seikei, Tokyo, Strasbourg, and the EPHE under Georges Dumézil. A scholar of religious studies and archaeology, he worked at CNRS (~1964–1969) and was a professor at Seikei University (1970) and Gakushuin University (2006).

Atsuki Nakagami works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakagami served as a visiting researcher at the University of Hamburg (attested 2022) and held research affiliations attested through the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2026.
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1989) and became a professor at Toyo University around 2004.

Atsushi Kanazawa studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1981). Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he lectured at the Meteorological College (~1986–1993) and held faculty positions at Komazawa University from ~1993.

Atsushi Kiyozawa works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi (~1980–1986) and served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

Atsushi Uno studied at Kyoto University and Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. A scholar of Indology and philosophy, he held posts at Shuchiin, Tokai, Hiroshima (professor 1974–1986), and Kindai University (professor ~1986–1996).
